# ReadonlyPropertyReassignment

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> <Badge type="info" text="PHP ≥ 8.1" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Detect assignment to a resolved readonly instance property already initialized on every reachable incoming path.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
class Item { public readonly int $id; public function __construct() {$this->id=1; $this->id=2;} }
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Initialize this readonly property only once.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report assignment to a resolved readonly instance property already initialized on every reachable incoming path.
- Every writing assignment operator counts as a repeated write: plain `=` and the compound operators (`+=`, `-=`, `.=`, ...) all fail on an initialized readonly property. The null-coalescing assignment `??=` is the exception, see E3.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is enabled, with positive proof required.
- For flow-dependent conditions, require a reachable source-to-use path with no intervening invalidation. Unknown calls, ambiguous aliases, recursion or analysis-budget exhaustion cannot establish definite facts.

## Exceptions (no report)

- A first permitted initialization, version-permitted clone reinitialization, unknown initialization state and reflection operations are excluded.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.

- E3. A `??=` assignment is never reported. It writes only when the stored value is null, and the adjacent-assignment proof establishes that the property is initialized, not that it holds null; on a non-null value the statement is a no-op and PHP raises nothing.

## Fix

No automatic fix: removing an assignment may conceal a missing design change.

## PHP versions

Available from PHP 8.1. Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Options

None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ReadonlyPropertyReassignment": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore ReadonlyPropertyReassignment
```
